title: The Core Idea: Airflow DAGs & Dependencies

scenes.say: How does Airflow know what to run, and in what order? Let's break down the core idea.

scenes.label: DAG
scenes.sub: Directed Acyclic Graph defines workflow steps
scenes.say: In Airflow, the backbone is the D A G—a Directed Acyclic Graph. It maps out every step in your workflow.
You create tasks for each step, pick operators for what they do, and set dependencies to control the run order.
You link tasks using double greater-than or set_upstream. This tells Airflow exactly what runs after what.

scenes.question: Can tasks run in any order in a DAG?
scenes.right: No. You must define dependencies so tasks run in the right order.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: Can tasks run in any order in a D A G? No—they only run in the order you define with dependencies.
